name: bbox-filemaker-plugin
description: Use this skill whenever the user is writing FileMaker calculations, scripts, or script steps that call the bBox plug-in (functions or script steps prefixed bBox_ or 'bBox ...'), or asks to shell out, run AppleScript, Python, Ruby, Node/JavaScript, cURL, DuckDB/SQLite, GraphicsMagick, or manipulate files/pasteboard/webviewers from within FileMaker. Also use for bBox installation, licensing/download, error handling (bBox_LastError), mode parameters, session/thread-safety questions, or PSoS/Server-side script limitations involving bBox.
summary: bBox is a free FileMaker plug-in that acts as a toolbox of native functions and script steps, letting FileMaker solutions on macOS or Ubuntu Server call out to AppleScript, shell/Bash/Zsh, cURL (SOAP/REST), DuckDB and SQLite, JavaScript (Node and JavaScriptCore), JQ, GraphicsMagick, Python, Ruby, and XPath, plus OS-level features like the pasteboard, file system, WebViewer control, and syslog. It fills gaps in FileMaker's built-in calculation/script-step vocabulary so developers can avoid workarounds for things like JSON/XML parsing, SOAP calls, PDF/Excel generation, image manipulation, or shelling out to external code libraries.
when_to_use: Writing or debugging a FileMaker calculation/script that calls any bBox_* function or 'bBox ...' script step

Deciding which bBox function fits a task (shell command, HTTP/REST/SOAP call, Python/Ruby/Node execution, image processing, file I/O, pasteboard/clipboard, AppleScript automation, WebViewer JS injection, DuckDB/SQLite queries)
Installing or upgrading the bBox plug-in on macOS, FileMaker Server, or Ubuntu 20/22/24 (client or server)
Handling bBox errors via bBox_LastError, or troubleshooting a function that isn't returning expected results
Understanding a function's mode parameter, session/reference handling, or thread-safety constraints
Evaluating whether a bBox function will work under PSoS (Perform Script on Server), server schedules, WebDirect, or inside a stored vs. unstored calculation field

platform_support.filemaker_versions: FileMaker Client and Server 21 - 26.x (basic compatibility checked back to FileMaker 21.0; older versions may still work)
notes: Ubuntu support was added in bBox 0.98.06; Apple Silicon (M1) support in 0.98.07; Ubuntu ARM in 1.05.
There is no Windows version of the plug-in.

On Linux, several functions have extra OS-level dependencies that must be installed or the plug-in will fail to load: bBox_GraphicsMagick, bBox_JavaScript (function and script step), bBox_JQ, bBox_Python / bBox_Python3Run (function and script step), bBox_Ruby, bBox_Zsh.
On macOS, most Python functions except for bBox_Python3Run are hard-linked to the official Python 3.13.x binaries from python.org.

installation.how_to_get_it: Free download via a request form at https://beezwax.net/forms/download/bbox (no info required, contact info optional/helpful).
installation.client_install: Drop the plug-in file into a container field and run the Install Plug-In File script step, or place it manually in <home>/Library/Application Support/FileMaker/FileMaker Pro/{version}/ on macOS.
installation.server_install: Server-side install requires the 'FileMaker Script Engine Plug-ins' option and 'Install Plug-in File' script step option enabled in FMS Admin Console. See Claris' plug-in management docs. Server-side use limits functions that need a logged-in user/UI (notably much AppleScript functionality).
installation.version_check_tip: Check for an existing install by testing whether bBox_Version returns '?' before reinstalling, to avoid needless re-installs.

ubuntu_install.general: Copy the bBox.fmx file to /opt/FileMaker/FileMaker Server/Database Server/Extensions/ and ensure FMS has access (chown fmserver:fmsadmin, or fmserver: on Ubuntu 24). Restart the script engine after upgrades with: fmsadmin restart fmse
ubuntu_install.ubuntu_20: Python 3.11 isn't available by default; add the deadsnakes PPA, then: sudo apt-get -y install libpython3.11 libjavascriptcoregtk-4.0-18 libobjc4
ubuntu_install.ubuntu_22: sudo apt-get -y install libpython3.11 libjavascriptcoregtk-4.1 (intel & ARM; use the Ubuntu 20 .fmx)
ubuntu_install.ubuntu_24: Add the deadsnakes PPA for Python 3.11, then: sudo apt-get -y install libpython3.11 libjavascriptcoregtk-4.1-0 libobjc4 (intel & ARM; use the Ubuntu 22 .fmx)

installation.demo_file: The bBox Plug-in Demo file (requires FileMaker Pro/Server 20.0+) auto-installs/updates the plug-in on macOS and contains ~200 example functions.

known_limitations: Server-side scripts (PSoS/schedules) cannot use functions that depend on a logged-in user or launching/communicating with a GUI application (e.g. much of AppleScript).
FMS's script engine is more resource-constrained; heavy native code (e.g. large Python loops pushing data onto the stack) can exceed stack limits and crash the script engine.
FileMaker limits PSoS parameters/results to 1,000,000 characters; exceeding this can hang the client.
Shell, Bash, Python, and Ruby-based functions do not behave reliably inside a STORED calculation field; use unstored calculations instead.

bBox_Shell only returns stdout, and does not support container data as its script parameter; use bBox_Bash or bBox_Zsh for finer control over input/output. bBox_Shell output is truncated after 160 MB.

core_concepts.mode_parameter: Many bBox functions/script steps take a leading 'mode' integer that toggles behavior (e.g. for bBox_Shell: 0 = convert both input/output line endings, 1 = skip CR-to-LF conversion of FileMaker input, 2 = skip LF-to-CR conversion of shell output, 3 = skip both conversions). Always check the specific function's mode table rather than assuming 0 is always the same meaning across functions. See the 'Mode Parameters' wiki page.
core_concepts.error_handling: Use bBox_LastError(reference) to retrieve the last error for a given engine/category (e.g. 'posix' for shell-family functions). Reference-based functions (DuckDB, SQLite, XPath, Python sessions) generally report errors scoped to their reference/session.
core_concepts.references_and_sessions: Stateful integrations (bBox_DuckDBOpen/Exec/Close, bBox_SQLiteOpen/Exec/Close, bBox_PythonCompile/Execute/GetVar/SetVar/Finalize, bBox_XPathInitializeFromText/Evaluate/Finalize) use an open/execute/close (or compile/execute/finalize) lifecycle keyed by a reference number, and have thread-safety rules — consult 'Sessions and Thread Safety' before running these concurrently or across scripts/threads.
core_concepts.native_bridge_classes: bBox_JavaScript, bBox_JavaScriptNode, and the Python execution functions can expose an `fm` class/object inside the script environment, letting embedded Python/JavaScript code call back into FileMaker (get/set fields, run scripts, etc.). See 'Native Python, JavaScript, and DuckDB Functions', 'Python Native Functions', and 'JavaScript Native Functions'.
core_concepts.functions_vs_script_steps: Most functions have an equivalent script step that calls the same underlying code, sometimes with simplified parameters. For complex scenarios prefer the function form; use the script step for simple cases or when a step-based workflow is more convenient.

functions.name: bBox_Shell
functions.description: Executes the given text with the Unix shell and returns stdout only (max 2 GB, truncated after 160 MB). Does not support container data as the script parameter; for more control over input/output use bBox_Bash or bBox_Zsh instead.

parameters.mode: 0 = convert both input and output line endings; 1 = skip converting FileMaker's carriage-return line endings to newlines on input; 2 = skip converting shell newline output back to carriage returns; 3 = skip translation of input and output line endings entirely
parameters.script: String to be evaluated (executed) by the shell

functions.result: String returned from executing the shell command

functions.name: bBox_Bash
functions.description: Runs text as a Bash script with more control over input/output/parameters than bBox_Shell, including container-data support.

functions.name: bBox_Zsh
functions.description: Runs text as a Zsh script, analogous to bBox_Bash but using the Z shell.

functions.name: bBox_Applescript
functions.signature: bBox_Applescript ( mode ; script {; handler ; param1 ; param2} )
functions.description: Executes AppleScript, optionally calling a specific handler with parameters. macOS only; limited when run server-side (PSoS) because there is no accessible logged-in GUI session.

functions.name: bBox_Curl
functions.description: Performs HTTP requests (GET/POST/etc.) via cURL, commonly used for REST and SOAP web-service calls from FileMaker.

functions.name: bBox_CurrentTime
functions.description: Returns the current time, optionally in a specified format (higher precision than FileMaker's native Get(CurrentTime)).

functions.name: bBox_DoScript
functions.description: Invokes a script in another (or the same) FileMaker file by name, optionally passing a parameter.

functions.name: bBox_DuckDBOpen
functions.description: Opens a DuckDB database file (or in-memory database) and returns a reference used by bBox_DuckDBExec / bBox_DuckDBClose.

functions.name: bBox_DuckDBExec
functions.description: Executes a SQL statement against an open DuckDB reference, optionally with bound parameters.

functions.name: bBox_DuckDBClose
functions.description: Closes a DuckDB reference opened with bBox_DuckDBOpen.

functions.name: bBox_Scp
functions.description: Transfers files to/from a remote host over SCP.

functions.name: bBox_SQLiteOpen
functions.description: Opens a SQLite database and returns a reference for bBox_SQLiteExec / bBox_SQLiteOptions / bBox_SQLiteClose. Used on older bBox versions in place of DuckDB.

functions.name: bBox_SQLiteExec
functions.description: Executes a SQL statement against an open SQLite reference.

functions.name: bBox_SQLiteOptions
functions.description: Sets the column/row separators used when formatting SQLite result sets as text.

functions.name: bBox_SQLiteClose
functions.description: Closes a SQLite reference opened with bBox_SQLiteOpen.

functions.name: bBox_ExecuteSQL
functions.signature: bBox_ExecuteSQL ( filename ; sqlQuery {; columnSeparator ; rowSeparator ; arguments ...} )
functions.description: Runs a SQL query directly against a file path (e.g. a SQLite/DuckDB file) without a persistent open reference.

functions.name: bBox_JavaScript
functions.description: Evaluates a JavaScript expression using JavaScriptCore, optionally exposing an `fm` bridge object back to FileMaker. Requires libjavascriptcoregtk on Ubuntu.

functions.name: bBox_JavaScriptNode
functions.description: Runs JavaScript using a Node.js engine rather than JavaScriptCore, for access to the Node ecosystem/APIs.

functions.name: bBox_Python3Run
functions.description: Runs a Python 3 script in a fresh interpreter invocation (simpler, non-persistent alternative to the Compile/Execute/GetVar/SetVar/Finalize session-based Python functions). Has special Linux dependency requirements.

functions.name: bBox_PythonCompile
functions.description: Compiles Python code into a persistent interpreter session, paired with bBox_PythonExecute / bBox_PythonEval / bBox_PythonGetVar / bBox_PythonSetVar / bBox_PythonFinalize.

functions.name: bBox_PythonExecute
functions.description: Executes the previously compiled Python session code.

functions.name: bBox_PythonEval
functions.description: Evaluates a Python expression within an existing Python session/reference and returns its value.

functions.name: bBox_PythonGetVar
functions.description: Retrieves the value of a variable from the active Python session.

functions.name: bBox_PythonSetVar
functions.description: Sets a variable's value in the active Python session, optionally specifying its Python type.

functions.name: bBox_PythonFinalize
functions.description: Tears down/finalizes the active Python session started with bBox_PythonCompile.

functions.name: bBox_Ruby
functions.signature: bBox_Ruby ( mode ; text ; param1 {; param2 ; ... ; param5} )
functions.description: Executes a Ruby script, analogous to bBox_Bash/bBox_Python3Run for the Ruby interpreter.

functions.name: bBox_JQ
functions.description: Runs a jq filter/expression against JSON text — useful for JSON transformations beyond FileMaker's native JSON functions.

functions.name: bBox_EvaluateList
functions.description: Evaluates a calculation expression once per item in a delimited list of values, useful for list-based transformations.

functions.name: bBox_Grep
functions.signature: bBox_Grep ( mode ; text ; param1 {; param2 ; param3} )
functions.description: Searches/extracts text using regular expressions (grep-style pattern matching).

functions.name: bBox_SplitText
functions.signature: bBox_SplitText ( text ; position ; length ; skipRepeats ; separator1 ; separator2 ; delimiter )
functions.description: Splits text into components based on position/length and separator rules.

functions.name: bBox_ParsePositionList
functions.description: Parses a position list (as used for layout element XML) for ad-hoc searches of layout elements.

functions.name: bBox_GetCharacterStyle
functions.description: Returns character-level style information (e.g. font/format) at a given position in styled text.

functions.name: bBox_Sort
functions.signature: bBox_Sort ( mode ; input ; param1 {; param2 ; param3} )
functions.description: Sorts a list of values according to the given mode and parameters.

functions.name: bBox_FileRead
functions.description: Reads a file from disk as text or container data, with optional byte offset and target filename for the container result.

functions.name: bBox_FileWrite
functions.description: Writes text or container data to a file on disk, optionally appending rather than overwriting.

functions.name: bBox_FileStatus
functions.description: Returns status/metadata information about a file or directory path (existence, size, permissions, etc. depending on parameter).

functions.name: bBox_FileSymLink
functions.description: Creates a symbolic link (or optionally a hard link) between two file paths.

functions.name: bBox_MimeTypeForPath
functions.description: Returns the MIME type inferred for a given file path.

functions.name: bBox_GraphicsMagick
functions.description: Performs image conversion/manipulation using GraphicsMagick. Requires extra OS dependencies on Ubuntu.

functions.name: bBox_Sips
functions.description: Performs image conversion/manipulation using macOS's built-in sips tool (macOS only).

functions.name: bBox_PasteboardFlavors
functions.description: Lists the data flavors/types currently available on the system pasteboard (clipboard).

functions.name: bBox_PasteboardGet
functions.description: Retrieves data of a given flavor/type from the system pasteboard.

functions.name: bBox_PasteboardSet
functions.description: Writes data of a given flavor/type to the system pasteboard.

functions.name: bBox_PerformKeystrokes
functions.description: Simulates keyboard input to the active application (macOS UI automation).

functions.name: bBox_MacCalendar
functions.description: Reads or manipulates macOS Calendar (EventKit) data.

functions.name: bBox_MacNotificationsGetSettings
functions.description: Returns the current macOS notification settings for the application.

functions.name: bBox_SetEnvironmentVariable
functions.description: Sets an OS environment variable visible to subsequently launched child processes (e.g. shell/Python/Ruby calls).

functions.name: bBox_SysCtl
functions.description: Reads low-level system control (sysctl) values from the OS.

functions.name: bBox Text Window Action
functions.signature: bBox Text Window Action [ destination ; reference ; operation ; parameter1 ; parameter2 )
functions.description: Set, get, or perform action on a previously created text window. Operations include setting the window title, getting or setting the selection range, getting contents as text or HTML, or setting the window title. macOS only.

functions.name: bBox Text Window Open
functions.signature: bBox Text Window Open [ destination ; title ; input type ; frame ]
functions.description: Create a new text window. macOS only.

functions.name: bBox_WebViewLoadHTML
functions.description: Loads raw HTML content into a named WebViewer object on a layout.

functions.name: bBox_WebViewLoadFile
functions.description: Loads a local file into a named WebViewer object.

functions.name: bBox_WebViewEvaluateJavaScript
functions.signature: bBox_WebViewEvaluateJavaScript ( window ; webviewer ; script {; handlerFileName ; handlerScriptName} )
functions.description: Runs JavaScript inside a WebViewer, optionally calling back into a FileMaker script/handler with the result.

functions.name: bBox_WebViewIsLoading
functions.description: Returns whether a WebViewer is currently loading content.

functions.name: bBox_WebViewEstimatedProgress
functions.description: Returns the estimated load progress (0-1) of a WebViewer.

functions.name: bBox_WebViewTitle
functions.description: Returns the page title currently loaded in a WebViewer.

functions.name: bBox_XPathInitializeFromText
functions.description: Loads XML text into an XPath context (with optional namespace bindings) for querying with bBox_XPathEvaluate.

functions.name: bBox_XPathEvaluate
functions.description: Evaluates an XPath expression against the XML loaded by bBox_XPathInitializeFromText.

functions.name: bBox_XPathFinalize
functions.description: Releases the XPath context created by bBox_XPathInitializeFromText.

functions.name: bBox_URLHandlerInfo
functions.description: Returns information about which application registers/handles a given URL scheme.

functions.name: bBox_FM_API_URL
functions.description: Returns a URL usable for calling FileMaker's own Data/Admin API from within the current session/context.

functions.name: bBox_Version
functions.description: Returns the installed bBox plug-in version, or '?' if bBox is not installed/registered — useful as an install-check before triggering an installation step.

functions.name: bBox_LastError
functions.description: Returns the last error for a given function family/reference (e.g. "posix" for shell-type calls, or a session/reference number for stateful engines).

functions.name: bBox_ReferenceInfo
functions.description: Returns diagnostic information about an open reference (DuckDB/SQLite/XPath/Python session, etc.).

functions.name: bBox_SessionInfo
functions.description: Returns diagnostic information about the current bBox session.

functions.name: bBox_ThreadInfo
functions.description: Returns diagnostic information about the current execution thread — useful when debugging thread-safety issues with stateful bBox functions.

functions.name: bBox_StackBacktrace
functions.description: Returns a stack backtrace for debugging plug-in crashes or hangs.

functions.name: bBox Syslog
functions.description: Script step writes log entries to the system syslog; related script steps include Syslog Open/Close for managing a persistent log handle.

functions.name: bBox Schema Notifications
functions.signature: bBox Schema Notifications [ type ; pathOrURL ; Script Name ; Credentials ]
functions.description: Registers a script to receive notifications when the FileMaker schema changes, optionally routed to a path/URL such as syslog or DuckDB, per the plug-in API.

usage_notes_for_assistant: Function names use FileMaker calculation syntax with semicolons separating parameters, e.g. bBox_Shell ( mode ; script ). Do not convert semicolons to commas when writing FileMaker calculations.

Not every function listed on the wiki has a corresponding public wiki page yet — some link out to beezwax.net product pages instead; treat those as authoritative for parameter details not captured here.

This file summarizes documentation retrieved on 2026-07-06 from a live wiki (48 pages); the wiki is actively edited, so re-check https://github.com/beezwax/bbox-documentation/wiki for the latest signatures, mode tables, and version notes before giving precise parameter-by-parameter guidance on a less-common function.

When a user's environment is Ubuntu Server, always check the 'platform_support.notes' Linux dependency list before suggesting bBox_Python3Run, bBox_Ruby, bBox_JQ, bBox_JavaScript, bBox_Zsh, or bBox_GraphicsMagick, since these fail to load without extra system libraries.
When a user reports a bBox function silently failing inside a calculation field, check first whether it's a STORED calculation — Shell/Bash/Python/Ruby-family functions require unstored calculations.
